description: Registers an existing repository folder as a Polarion project (the inverse of `unmarkProject`): `requestBody` names the repository `location`, the new `projectId`, its `trackerPrefix`, and optionally a `templateId`. Runs as an asynchronous job and returns a `jobs` resource; poll `getJob` until it finishes. Use it to re-attach project data that already exists in the repository; to create a brand-new project use `createProject`. Effect: triggers a server-side action rather than a plain resource creation — whether repeating it is safe, a no-op, or rejected depends on the specific action; treat it as not guaranteed idempotent. Tip: set `dry_run: true` first to validate the arguments and preview the exact request without sending it to Polarion. The executor returns this preview as normal text, and as structured content when the tool declares an output schema.

dry_run.description: If true, validates the request and returns the exact request that would be sent to Polarion — with the Authorization header redacted and any binary payload summarized by byte length — without actually sending it.

location.description: Location of the new Project to be created.

params.description: Parameters of new Project to be created.

projectId.description: Id of the new Project to be created.

templateId.description: Id of the template to create the new Project from.

trackerPrefix.description: Tracker prefix of the new Project to be created.

name: markProject
